questions.stem: The strict enclosed physical area of a large geometric rectangle is exactly 252 sq cm and its actual length and breadth are purely in the numerical ratio of precisely 9:7 respectively. What exactly is its total outer perimeter?
questions.explanation: Let length be 9x and breadth be 7x. Area = length * breadth = 9x * 7x = 63x² = 252. Therefore x² = 252/63 = 4, so x = 2. Length = 18 cm, Breadth = 14 cm. Perimeter = 2(L + B) = 2(18 + 14) = 2(32) = 64 cm.

questions.stem: Accurately strictly find the total surface internal area of a precise right-angled physical triangle whose flat solid base is exactly 12 cm and whose absolute longest hypotenuse is exactly 13 cm.
questions.explanation: Using Pythagoras theorem: Height² = Hypotenuse² - Base² = 13² - 12² = 169 - 144 = 25. Height = 5 cm. Area = 1/2 * base * height = 1/2 * 12 * 5 = 30 sq cm.

questions.stem: A long flexible metal wire when perfectly bent firmly in the strict form of a physical square smoothly encloses a total internal area of exactly 484 sq cm. What exactly will be the precise enclosed internal area when the completely identical wire is perfectly completely bent smoothly into the strict form of a perfect circle?
questions.explanation: Area of square = 484, so side = √484 = 22 cm. Length of wire (perimeter) = 4 * 22 = 88 cm. When bent into a circle, circumference = 2πr = 88. 2 * (22/7) * r = 88 => 44r/7 = 88 => r = 14 cm. Area of circle = πr² = (22/7) * 14 * 14 = 616 sq cm.

questions.stem: The strict physical internal diagonal of a perfectly geometric rectangle is exactly √(41) cm and its absolute internal exact area is precisely 20 sq cm. The true outer physical perimeter of the specific geometric rectangle absolutely formally must securely be:
questions.explanation: L² + B² = (Diagonal)² = 41. Area LB = 20. We use the identity (L+B)² = L² + B² + 2LB = 41 + 2(20) = 41 + 40 = 81. Therefore, L+B = 9. Perimeter = 2(L+B) = 2 * 9 = 18 cm.

questions.stem: If the perfect formal rigid physical radius of a geometric circle is explicitly aggressively mathematically increased by precisely 50%, its absolute internal total strict area is ultimately correctly strongly firmly effectively increased by:
questions.explanation: If radius increases by 50%, new radius R = 1.5r. New area = πR² = π(1.5r)² = 2.25πr². The new area is 2.25 times the original area, which is an increase of 1.25 times, or 125%.

questions.stem: The horizontal strict straight flat firm base of a geometrical physical parallelogram is physically strictly entirely completely twice its vertical rigid exact height. If the total internal exact area of the parallelogram is precisely 72 sq cm, mathematically find its vertical strictly exact height.
questions.explanation: Let height be h. Base = 2h. Area of parallelogram = Base * Height = (2h) * h = 2h². Given Area = 72. So 2h² = 72 => h² = 36 => h = 6 cm.

questions.stem: Exactly four identical equal physical geometric circles are thoroughly strictly described formally directly about the exactly four solid outer corners of a formal rigid square so that each perfectly externally formally touches strictly exactly two of the others. If a firm flat side of the square is 14 cm, then the exact specific internal bounded blank area safely smoothly enclosed purely perfectly exactly between the strict outer formal boundaries of the circles is:
questions.explanation: The side of the square is 14 cm. The circles touch each other, so the radius of each circle is 14/2 = 7 cm. Area of the square = 14 * 14 = 196 sq cm. The four corners of the square contain four quarter-circles, which together make one full circle of radius 7 cm. Area of this full circle = πr² = (22/7) * 7² = 154 sq cm. Enclosed area between the circles = Area of square - Area of the four quarter-circles = 196 - 154 = 42 sq cm.
